deep.reconstruction:
Context: π = π_{0,3}, the (profinite) fundamental group of P^1_C − {0,1,∞}, with loop generators l_0, l_1, l_∞ and l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1. The previous page found that S_3 acts on π only by outer automorphisms: ρ is the 3-cycle l_0→l_1→l_∞→l_0, and σ_0σ_1 = int(l_1^{-1})ρ, etc.

This page does three things.

(1) Complex conjugation. It adds complex conjugation τ to the extended Teichmüller group Γ_{0,3}, given explicitly by τ(l_0) = l_0^{-1}, τ(l_1) = l_1^{-1}, τ(l_∞) = l_1 l_0 = int(l_1) l_∞^{-1}.
- This is a genuine automorphism: l_0^{-1} l_1^{-1} l_1 l_0 = 1.
- It sends each l_i to a conjugate of l_i^{-1}, so it is an automorphism 'à lacets' of signature (multiplier) −1.
- It satisfies τ^2 = 1.
- τ commutes with S_3 modulo inner automorphisms. This is consistent with the Möbius maps permuting 0, 1, ∞ having real coefficients. One checks that τρτρ^{-1} = int(l_1).
- Hence the outer action of S_3 × {±1} = Γ_{0,3} on π is the canonical one, the extended mapping class group of the thrice-punctured sphere.

(2) Normalising an outer automorphism. Grothendieck turns to outer automorphisms (of loop type) that commute with the S_3-action, i.e. with ρ (the image reads 'commutent à ρ', not τ). Any such outer automorphism preserving the conjugacy class of L_0 = ⟨l_0⟩ ≅ Ẑ lifts to an automorphism u normalising L_0. This lift is unique up to int(λ), λ ∈ L_0, because the normaliser of L_0 in the free profinite group is L_0 itself. With p = χ(u) ∈ Ẑ* the multiplier ('cyclotomic character'), we get (*) u(l_0) = l_0^p.

(3) The defect g. Since u commutes with ρ modulo inner automorphisms, there is a unique g ∈ π̂ (the centre is trivial) with (**) uρ = int(g)ρu.

On the next page this gives:
- u(l_1) = int(g) l_1^p and u(l_∞) = int(gρ(g)) l_∞^p.
- The relation l_0^p g l_1^p ρ(g) l_∞^p ρ(g)^{-1} g^{-1} = 1. This is a 'hexagon'-type (3-cycle) condition on the pair (p, g).

This is a parametrisation by pairs (multiplier, group element) of automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} compatible with Γ_{0,3}. It is exactly the type of parametrisation later made into the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group by Drinfeld (1990), with (λ, f) and relations I (2-cycle, which τ/σ will furnish) and II (3-cycle, the hexagon). Grothendieck's normalisation differs: he takes u(l_1) = g l_1^p g^{-1} with g the ρ-defect, whereas Drinfeld takes y ↦ f^{-1} y^λ f with f ∈ F̂_2'. The aim is to describe the image of Gal(Q̄/Q) in Out(π̂_{0,3}) and its compatibility with the Teichmüller tower.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The formula τ(l_∞) = l_1 l_0 = int(l_1) l_∞^{-1} checks out, and τ is a well-defined involution.
The commutation of τ with S_3 modulo inner automorphisms is only asserted ('On vérifie'). It does hold, e.g. τρτρ^{-1} = int(l_1).
The uniqueness of u mod L_0-conjugation tacitly uses that the normaliser of ⟨l_0⟩ in π̂ is ⟨l_0⟩ itself. This is true for a primitive element of a free profinite group, but it is not stated.
Notation clash: ρ denotes the 3-cycle, while the multiplier is written p (= χ(u)). The machine transcription conflates the two.

ideas.what: Complex conjugation as an explicit involutive automorphism of π_{0,3} of multiplier −1, giving Γ_{0,3} = S_3 × {±1} acting by outer automorphisms
ideas.modern_name: Extended mapping class group of M_{0,3}; complex conjugation in GT theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; in the GT setting Drinfeld 1990, Ihara
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions the extended Teichmüller groups and complex conjugation in general terms

ideas.what: Lifting an S_3-compatible outer automorphism to u with u(l_0) = l_0^p (unique mod L_0) and encoding the failure to commute with ρ by g ∈ π̂ (uρ = int(g)ρu)
ideas.modern_name: Parametrisation of Ĝ T by pairs (λ, f) ∈ Ẑ* × F̂_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990; Ihara (Galois action via (χ, f_σ)), Belyi 1979 for faithfulness

ideas.what: The resulting 3-cycle (hexagon) condition l_0^p g l_1^p ρ(g) l_∞^p ρ(g)^{-1} g^{-1} = 1 (computed on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Relation II (hexagon) of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group

missed.claim: In spring 1981 Grothendieck sets up the explicit description of automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} compatible with Γ_{0,3} = S_3 × {±1}. Each is given by a multiplier p ∈ Ẑ* plus an element g ∈ π̂ measuring the defect of commutation with the 3-cycle. This is the germ of the (λ, f)-parametrisation of Ĝ T and of the hexagon relation, nine years before Drinfeld. His normalisation differs: g is the ρ-defect with u(l_1) = g l_1^p g^{-1}.
missed.quote: Soit g ∈ π tel que (**) uρ = int(g)ρu, ce qui détermine g de façon unique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents precisely how far Grothendieck went towards GT before Drinfeld/Ihara. His alternative normalisation via the S_3 (ρ, τ) symmetry might give a slightly different but equivalent presentation, of interest to the history of GT. The broad anticipation is known to specialists (Lochak–Schneps et al.), so the novelty is in the detail.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains no finished new theorem. However, it shows an explicit, pre-Drinfeld computational set-up of GT-type relations, with complex conjugation and the S_3 symmetry built in. Grothendieck's general anticipation of GT is well known, but this level of explicit parametrisation in 1981 is a notable unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: (**) reads 'uρ = int(g) ρ u' (with ρ the 3-cycle, over a crossed-out term), not 'uτ = int(g)τ u'. This is consistent with the next page's use u(l_1) = uρ(l_0).
'Si ρ ∈ Ẑ*' should read 'Si p (= χ(u)) ∈ Ẑ*'; the multiplier is p, and (*) is u(l_0) = l_0^p.
'autom. extérieurs qui commutent à τ' most likely reads 'commutent à ρ'.
The inserted phrase 'qui normalise la classe de conj. de l_0' attaches to 'tout autom. extérieur', i.e. every outer automorphism preserving the conjugacy class of l_0 lifts to u normalising L_0.
